articles.title: DialFork: a benchmark for procedural hallucination in conversational agents [R]
articles.summary: Hi all, author here (Idiap Research Institute, joint work with Logitech). We recently released DialFork and thought it might interest people here. It's a benchmark for a failure mode of LLM agents that is easy to miss: every turn is fluent and factual, the tool calls are correct, yet the agent stops following the procedure it was given. For example, asked for the weather, it fetches the forecast (correct tool call) but never tells you, and starts asking you to rate its service instead. Most steps of a conversational procedure aren't tool calls but things the agent has to say: asking, confirming, telling the result. When an agent drifts from these steps, we call it procedural hallucination: a third axis, alongside factual accuracy and correct tool use, and one that has been largely overlooked. To our knowledge, DialFork is the first benchmark aimed at measuring this axis: what the agent has to say, and in what order. How it's built: we simulate dialogues where an agent follows its workf
